River 1.0 is the first network PyMC Labs has trained and published for PyMC MFM. It
reads one weekly series of media spend, controls and outcome, with any number of
channels and up to 10 controls, and returns posterior draws of every component (baseline,
channels, controls, latent and indirect effects) together with the causal graph sampled
for each draw. Nothing is fitted to your data: `add_context` loads the history and the
weights stay as published.

![River 1.0: many weekly series, one amortized network.](river.svg){fig-alt="Abstract palette lines flow together across a rounded navy background, representing the River 1.0 model." width="72%" fig-align="center"}

It ships as the profile `river-1` of the Hugging Face repository `pymc-labs/mfm`. The
profile name is an identifier, not a version number.

## Install and load

Use Python 3.13 or newer. The Hub repository is currently private to the PyMC
Labs organization. Authenticate with `hf auth login`; `HF_TOKEN` is an
alternative for environments that provide it.

```bash
pip install "pymc-mfm[hub] @ git+https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-mfm.git"
hf auth login
```

Load the profile at its pinned commit:

```python
from pymc_mfm import from_pretrained

model = from_pretrained("pymc-labs/mfm", profile="river-1", revision="970e6095f14824d7e25ecace7e20a47bebde35b8")
```

## Artifact specification

The committed quickstart prints the following model configuration; it records
this artifact rather than making a general product guarantee.

| Specification | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Parameters | 2,443,583 |
| Bundle | About 10 MB |
| Control slots | 10 |
| `d_model` | 128 |
| `n_layers` | 4 |
| `n_heads` | 8 |
| `d_ff` | 512 |
| `flow_hidden` | 256 |
| `n_demand` | 1 |

## Recorded timing

| Profile | World | Draws | Hardware | Device | Query | Context |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| River-1 | quickstart world | 1,000 | Apple M3 Max | CPU | 2.0 s | 3.2 s |
| River-1 | quickstart world | 1,000 | Apple M3 Max | MPS | 1.4 s | 2.3 s |

These are recorded measurements, not a general performance guarantee.

On an NVIDIA L4, warm `torch.compile` calls were approximately 1.4× as fast as
eager across four test inputs; the first compilation took 20–30 seconds.
Sampling stays eager unless a caller opts in, and compiling on CPU usually does
not speed it up.

## Quickstart and limits

The [River-1 quickstart](../../guide/examples/river_1_quickstart.ipynb)
demonstrates a simulated weekly dataset, an 80% context / 20% query split,
1,000 draws per window, context and query decompositions, contribution plots,
and conditional scenario sweeps.

- Context and query are separate marginals.
- Components exclude observation noise.
- Conditional scenarios are not identified causal lift.
- There is no PyPI package, and licenses have not yet been selected.
